at2.bio: ATM — Andrelita T. Myril — is a painter and visual artist, a graduate of ENARTS, Haiti's most renowned National School of Arts. Her mission: put the tools of art in everyone's hands — to grow each person's creativity, give the mind the escape it needs, and nurture human and mental balance. Her canvases — bold colors, moving rhythms, figures and abstractions — are windows onto the light of Haiti and the Caribbean.

ds.prd031_h: Consumer price index, by region and commune
ds.prd031_meta: 📄 Prices • Sources : IHSI — Institut Haïtien de Statistique et d'Informatique • confidence level B • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5 (textes officiels et simples données). Agrégat régional rattaché aux communes par Atmart.
ds.prd031_p: The IHSI consumer price index broken down into five regions and attached to the 140 communes: index level, monthly change and twelve-month change. This is the ONLY territorial granularity the Haitian price index has — no international source goes below the country. Warning: the 140 communes carry only FIVE distinct values, those of the regions. ds.prd032_meta: 📄 Prices • Sources : PAM (WFP) via OCHA HDX • confidence level B • CC BY-IGO 3.0
ds.prd032_p: The annual average price of seven staple foods across the nine markets monitored by WFP, in gourdes AND in dollars. What this product shows and no national average reveals: the same marmite of maize meal costs 291 gourdes in Jérémie and 700 in Ouanaminthe on 2024 average. And over twenty years it is multiplied by 10.8 in gourdes but only 3.5 in dollars — the gap is the currency's depreciation.
ds.prd033_h: Licensed financial institutions, and what the map does not show
ds.prd033_meta: 🏛 Public finances • Sources : BRH — supervision bancaire ; OpenStreetMap via HOT • confidence level B • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5 (textes officiels et simples données)
ds.prd033_p: The 26 institutions licensed by the BRH — banks, money transfer houses, bureaux de change, electronic payment, microfinance — with their head office, set against the names recorded by contributory mapping. EIGHT licensed institutions are named by NO point on the map: three transfer houses, three bureaux de change, two electronic payment providers. That is the more useful half, because it says where to go and look. Order of magnitude to keep in mind: the BRH counts 5,250 financial service providers in June 2024; the contributory map carries 474.
ds.prd034_meta: 🏛 Public finances • Sources : BRH — liste des caisses populaires agréées • confidence level B • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd034_p: The 58 credit unions licensed by the BRH (March 2025 list): name, acronym, licence number, commune of the head office, number of counters, federation. This is the ONLY official financial list that reaches the territory — for banks and money transfer houses the BRH publishes the head office only. 57 of 58 unions are attached to a commune, across 47 communes. No telephone, no e-mail: a territorial atlas has no need of them.
ds.prd035_meta: 🏛 Public finances • Sources : OpenStreetMap via HOT ; sigles agréés de la BRH • confidence level C • ODbL
ds.prd035_p: The cooperative finance points recorded by OpenStreetMap, recognised one by one: 30 credit unions or cooperatives and 13 microfinance points, named and located, across 26 communes. THIS IS NOT A CENSUS — the BRH licenses 58 credit unions and counts 108 service points. An object is kept only if its name declares it or if it carries an acronym licensed by the BRH on an object tagged as financial: the rule misses badly tagged credit unions, and that is the direction in which it must err. Solidarity mutuals are not here and cannot be: without a licence, without premises, often without a stable name.
ds.prd036_h: The licence of every published file
ds.prd036_meta: 📐 Method • Sources : Registre des sources et passeports juridiques d'Atmart • confidence level A • CC BY 4.0
ds.prd036_p: One line per file on the site: its licence, the sources it comes from, the attribution to carry, and the reason. THERE IS NOT ONE LICENCE BUT SEVERAL, and that is the point: eleven files go out under ODbL because they derive from OpenStreetMap, whose share-alike passes to redistributed derived databases; others fall under no licence at all, since article 5 of the Haitian decree of 12 October 2005 excludes official texts and simple data from copyright. Announcing CC BY everywhere would grant a right the source withholds; announcing ODbL everywhere would forbid without cause. The table is recomputed from the source register at every run.
ds.prd037_h: The Haitian diaspora — where it lives
ds.prd037_meta: 👥 Population • Sources : ONU DESA — International Migrant Stock 2024 • confidence level A • CC BY 3.0 IGO
ds.prd037_p: How many people BORN IN HAITI live in each country, from 1990 to 2024, by sex. Two million in 2024 against 521,000 in 1990 — nearly four times more in thirty-four years. The five main host countries: United States (798,000), Dominican Republic (535,000), Chile (172,000), France (117,000), Canada (107,000). THIS IS NOT « THE DIASPORA »: the count is by place of BIRTH, never by descent — a child born in Brooklyn to Haitian parents is not in it, so the lived diaspora is larger, by an amount this source cannot estimate. NOR IS IT COMMUNE-LEVEL DATA, and it will not become so: no line says which commune the person left.
ds.prd038_h: Forced returns to Haiti — entry points and profile
ds.prd038_meta: 👥 Population • Sources : OIM/DTM avec l'ONM et le GARR — Suivi des retours forcés vers Haïti • confidence level B • Conditions OIM/DTM — publication sous réserve, passeport PSP-066
ds.prd038_p: 270,214 people were forcibly returned to Haiti in 2025, 36% more than in 2024, including 265,215 from the Dominican Republic (98%). They enter through points that ARE communes: Belladère receives 51% of arrivals, Ouanaminthe 27%. The first commune-level map on this subject. The profile follows: 66% adult men, but in a single year women rose 92%, girls 152% and boys 133%; average age 34; 85% had left for economic reasons; 32% hold no identity document; 19% were already displaced inside Haiti before leaving. ONLY TWO COMMUNES carry a share, and the other 138 are not at zero: they are without data.
ds.prd039_h: Removals from the United States — Haiti and the Dominican Republic
ds.prd039_meta: 👥 Population • Sources : DHS — Office of Homeland Security Statistics, Key Homeland Security Metrics : Repatriations • confidence level A • Domaine public — œuvre du gouvernement fédéral américain
ds.prd039_p: A MONTHLY series since October 2009, by country and by type of return — 364 observations. Long enough and regular enough to read a trend and a break. THE WORD « REPATRIATION » COVERS FOUR MECHANISMS: formal removal, enforcement return, administrative return, and Title 42 public-health expulsion. Adding them up under the word « deportation » inverts the reading: Haiti counts 14,090 repatriations in 2022, but only 1,540 formal removals — 12,360 were Title 42 expulsions, with no immigration proceeding. The comparison with the Dominican Republic is telling: before 2020 it had four to nine times more formal removals than Haiti; since 2023 it climbs back to 4,170 while Haiti stays at 740.
ds.prd040_h: Places of worship mapped, by commune
ds.prd040_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : OpenStreetMap via Overpass API • confidence level B • ODbL 1.0 — partage à l'identique
ds.prd040_p: 3,142 places of worship attached to 121 communes out of 140: 2,533 Christian, 279 VODOU, 12 spiritualist, 4 Muslim, and 302 with no religion tag. THIS IS NOT A CENSUS but the state of the MAPPING — a pale commune is far more likely one nobody has surveyed than one where few people worship. VODOU GETS ITS OWN COLUMN because no Haitian administrative register records it: folding it into a total would erase what is rare about this data. The 302 objects with no declared religion are not placed with the Christian ones — putting them there because « it is likely in Haiti » would replace an observation with an assumption.
ds.prd041_h: Licensed radio and television stations, by commune
ds.prd041_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : CONATEL — liste des stations de radiodiffusion autorisées 2023-2024 • confidence level A • Données publiques — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd041_p: 807 stations LICENSED by CONATEL: 665 FM radios, 8 AM radios and 134 television stations, with their frequency, owner and city. 80 communes hold at least one. This is an ADMINISTRATIVE ACT, not contributory mapping: an absent station is not one nobody saw, it is one without a licence. THE OWNER IS PUBLISHED because a frequency is a conceded public good and the regulator publishes it itself. THE DOCUMENT CONTRADICTS ITSELF in three places — its headings announce 36 radios in Nippes, 20 television stations in Nord and 18 in Sud while its tables contain 35, 19 and 17 — and we publish what the tables contain, naming the gap.
ds.prd042_h: Haiti's digital audience — access and platforms
ds.prd042_meta: 📄 Numérique • Sources : Kepios / DataReportal — Digital 2026: Haiti ; Banque mondiale (WDI) • confidence level B • Valeurs citées — contenu sous droit d'auteur de Kepios Pte. Ltd.
ds.prd042_p: Fourteen markers on who is online in Haiti, on which platforms, and through which pipe. 4.69 million internet users at the end of 2025, or 39.3 % of the population — and 7.25 million people offline. Facebook reaches 38.4 % of adults, Instagram 6.7 %. THE FACT THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING: 0.3 FIXED broadband subscription per 100 people (World Bank) against MOBILE connections equivalent to 84.6 % of the population, 97.2 % of them on 3G or better — Haiti's digital audience is mobile, entirely. TWO SOURCES DISAGREE: the World Bank counts 47.9 % internet users in 2024, Kepios 39.3 % at the end of 2025, and we publish both without arbitrating. Kepios figures are CITED with attribution; none of their pages or charts is reproduced.
ds.prd043_h: Diaspora remittances — origin, destination, month by month
ds.prd043_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : BRH — statistiques de la balance des paiements • confidence level A • Données publiques haïtiennes — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd043_p: 3,371 observations: money received from abroad AND sent abroad, by country and by month, from October 2017 to May 2026, with the number of transactions and the average amount. The United States account for 79 % of what comes in. BUT HAITI ALSO SENDS, and its top destination is not the United States: it is the DOMINICAN REPUBLIC, at 52 % — in fiscal 2025 Haiti sent it 155.9 million and received only 150.4. The outbound transfer is three times the size of the inbound one ($590 against $181): these are neither the same people nor the same gesture. The sum of countries reproduces the total the central bank publishes across all 215 month × direction pairs. Six lines are REGIONS rather than countries, and a column says so.
ds.prd044_h: Where diaspora money lands — by department
ds.prd044_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : BRH — BRH-Infos à la loupe n° 1, avril 2024 • confidence level B • Données publiques haïtiennes — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd044_p: The ONLY official territorial breakdown of remittances that exists for Haiti: ten departments, received and sent, over three periods. Ouest receives 68 to 70 % of all the money; Grand'Anse receives 0.7 %. The ratio is NINETY-THREE TO ONE where the population ratio is ten to one — remittances do not redistribute, they concentrate. THE TRAP TO KNOW: the amount is recorded where the transfer is PAID OUT, not where the recipient lives — so the concentration also measures that of the payout network, as the central bank itself notes. NOTHING EXISTS AT COMMUNE LEVEL for remittances. The values are read back from the document's own chart labels and cross-checked against the totals it states in words: all five controls pass.
ds.prd045_h: Haiti's banking system — balance sheet, performance, territory
ds.prd045_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : BRH — supervision bancaire, rapports statistiques trimestriels • confidence level A • Données publiques haïtiennes — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd045_p: Forty quarters of prudential ratios, bank by bank, from December 2013 to March 2026: capital, non-performing loans, ROA, ROE, operating costs, productivity per employee. The series is public but lives inside a workbook of nearly four hundred sheets; here it is laid flat. NON-PERFORMING LOANS ARE NOTHING ALIKE FROM ONE BANK TO THE NEXT: from 0 % to 75 % of gross loans in March 2026 — a system average would hide exactly what needs to be seen. AND AN UNEXPECTED TERRITORIAL FIGURE: deposits split between the METROPOLITAN REGION (77 %) and PROVINCIAL TOWNS (23 %), by bank and by deposit type. This is not commune level — the central bank does not go lower.
ds.prd046_h: Where a remittance can be collected — by commune
ds.prd046_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : CAM Transfer — répertoire public des points de service • confidence level B • Agrégat recalculé — le répertoire d'origine n'est pas republié
ds.prd046_p: THE ONLY COMMUNE-LEVEL DATA THAT EXISTS ON REMITTANCES. The amounts do not go below the department, but the payout NETWORK does read commune by commune: 1,632 service points recorded, 1,624 matched (99.5 %), 114 communes covered out of 140. This is the missing piece of the argument — the central bank explains the concentration of amounts by the concentration of sub-agents, and the two can finally be looked at side by side. TWO WARNINGS THAT MATTER: this count covers ONE money transfer company out of six, so a commune at zero is not a commune without access; and we publish the COUNT, never the directory of sub-agents — measuring without filing people.
ds.prd047_h: Banking network and dollarisation — Haiti's teller window
ds.prd047_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : BRH — sommaire financier détaillé (indicateurs CAMEL) • confidence level A • Données publiques haïtiennes — décret du 12/10/2005, art. 5
ds.prd047_p: TWO HUNDRED AND TWO bank teller points for the whole country in September 2025: one service point for roughly 59,000 people. The regulator's official count, bank by bank, over ten quarters — with staff numbers, deposit and loan accounts, assets and loan portfolio. AND THE MONETARY FACT THAT RESHAPES EVERYTHING ELSE: 64.3 % of the system's deposits are not in gourdes. A country whose savings are mostly denominated in another country's currency does not steer its exchange rate like others do. The control: the SYSTEM column reproduces the sum of the banks across the seven additive quantities, at all ten dates.
ds.prd048_h: Households living on remittances — by department
ds.prd048_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : FAO — Data in Emergencies Monitoring (DIEM), tours 4 à 6 • confidence level C • CC BY 4.0
ds.prd048_p: THE TWO MEASURES DO NOT GIVE THE SAME RANKING, AND YOU NEED TO KNOW WHY BEFORE CONCLUDING ANYTHING FROM IT. Grand'Anse receives 0.7 % of the amounts but 4.5 % of its households have remittances as their main income source; Sud receives three and a half times more money per head and counts only 0.5 %. THESE GAPS PROBABLY DO NOT MEASURE DEPENDENCE: the central bank records the money WHERE IT IS PAID OUT, and payout network density tracks per-capita amounts at +0.79 across departments — the official map of the money is first a map of the teller windows. Excluding Port-au-Prince, amounts and dependence are no longer correlated at all (−0.27). On top of that, the FAO does not separate remittances from abroad from those sent within Haiti. Ten departments, three survey rounds from June 2023 to June 2024, three ranks of income source. WHAT THIS FIGURE IS NOT: the share of households that RECEIVE a remittance, which would be far higher. Phone survey, 135 to 900 households per department: a two-point gap means nothing.
ds.prd049_meta: 💰 Economy • Sources : CAM Transfer — répertoire public des points de service • confidence level B • Répertoire public repris avec attribution, sans les téléphones
ds.prd049_p: The 1,632 service points of one money transfer company, one per row, with their trading name, address and commune. 1,624 matched to a commune, 1,627 with an address. Where the map layer COUNTS the payout windows, this directory LOCATES them — useful for planning a distribution, measuring real accessibility, or simply a journey. THE PHONE NUMBER IS NOT INCLUDED: the source file carries one per point, often a personal mobile number, and an address tells you where a shop is while a number lets you reach someone. ONE COMPANY OUT OF SIX: this is not the directory of Haiti's payout points, it is one operator's, and the record is dated — a sub-agent network changes fast. The control: the directory and the map count the same thing across all 114 served communes.
ds.prd050_h: Health, education and living-conditions outcomes — DHS
ds.prd050_meta: 👥 Social • Sources : EMMUS / DHS Program — API des indicateurs • confidence level A • Libre d'usage, citation imposée par le producteur
ds.prd050_p: THE ATLAS KNEW WHERE THE SCHOOLS ARE; IT DID NOT KNOW WHETHER CHILDREN LEARN. It knew where the clinics are, not whether people are better off. Here are the outcomes carried on the map: 908 observations, TWENTY indicators, sixteen years, and twenty maps where there were two. Infant and under-five mortality, stunting, anaemia, vaccination, mosquito nets; women's literacy and population with no education; water, sanitation, electricity, charcoal cooking, earth floors; fertility, unmet need for family planning, union before 18, violence experienced, household decisions, women's work; registered births — across the 2000, 2006, 2012 and 2016 surveys. THESE TWENTY FILL THEMES THAT WERE MUTE: the atlas showed facilities and no outcome at all on water, energy, employment, housing, or the situation of women. They are drawn from the full base (PRD-055), which publishes 2,132. A CHILD IS THREE TIMES MORE LIKELY TO DIE BEFORE AGE ONE in the rest of the West (84 per thousand) than in Grand'Anse (28). THE MESH IS NEITHER THE COMMUNE NOR THE DEPARTMENT: the DHS splits the West into the metropolitan area and the rest of the West — finer than the department where it matters — and the outlines come from the DHS itself, we reconstructed nothing. THE LIMIT THAT COUNTS: the last survey dates from 2016-2017. This product says where Haiti stood BEFORE the security collapse, not where it stands now.
ds.prd051_h: What Haitians say — insecurity lived, institutions, wanting to leave
ds.prd051_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : LAPOP Lab, Vanderbilt University — AmericasBarometer 2023 • confidence level B • Valeurs citées — rapport public sous droit d'auteur de LAPOP Lab
ds.prd051_p: THE ATLAS MEASURED INSECURITY BY EVENTS, never by what people live through — and it had NOTHING on governance or justice. Sixteen measures answer that, from a May-June 2023 survey: the atlas's freshest source on these questions, where the health survey stops in 2016. FOUR IN FIVE HAITIANS (79 %) INTEND TO EMIGRATE — a record since the series began in 2006, and 69 % of them are aiming for the United States. 78 % have experienced food insecurity, up 36 points since 2012. 70 % rate insecurity the gravest problem, against 13 % for the economy. And two figures that surprise: 54 % trust the national police, recovered from its 2017 low, but only 24 % trust the electoral system. THIS PRODUCT IS NATIONAL AND WILL STAY SO: a telephone survey that excludes anyone without a mobile, a 6.6 % response rate — the lowest of the round's twenty-four countries — and only five strata. Nothing here can be mapped, and the entry says why.
ds.prd052_h: Public opinion by survey region — trust, corruption, security, migration
ds.prd052_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : LAPOP Lab, Vanderbilt University — AmericasBarometer Haïti • confidence level A • Licence par clic LAPOP — agrégats autorisés, usage commercial interdit
ds.prd052_p: 358 estimates computed FROM THE MICRODATA of the AmericasBarometer, waves 2016/17, 2021 and 2023: trust in the courts, parliament, police and elections; bribe solicitation; crime victimisation; feelings of insecurity; intention to emigrate. Every value carries ITS DESIGN-BASED CONFIDENCE INTERVAL, and that is not decoration: OF 52 REGIONAL GAPS TESTED, ONLY 27 ARE ESTABLISHED — elsewhere the intervals overlap and the geography is not proven. Publishing the five figures without them would tell the story of a map that does not exist. THE MESH IS THE SURVEY REGION, five sampling strata — neither commune nor department, which the sampling design does not make representative. COMMERCIAL USE IS FORBIDDEN by the licence: these values serve the Explorateur, which is free, never paid work. The survey files are not published and will not be; what is shared is the replication code.
ds.prd053_h: Haiti and the Dominican Republic — sixteen identical questions
ds.prd053_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : LAPOP Lab, Vanderbilt University — AmericasBarometer 2023 • confidence level B • Licence par clic LAPOP — agrégats autorisés, usage commercial interdit
ds.prd053_p: THE EXPLORATEUR'S FIRST CARIBBEAN COMPARISON, and it covers the two countries of one island. Sixteen identical questions in 2023, eleven established gaps. FOUR STRIKING RESULTS: the intention to emigrate separates the two countries by 39 points (78.5 against 39.7); trust in the head of government separates them by 39 points THE OTHER WAY (13.0 against 51.8); Haitians trust their police MORE than Dominicans trust theirs (58.6 against 32.8); and they are asked for bribes eight times less often (2.4 against 18.8). Crime victimisation, however, is almost identical (25.4 against 24.2) and the gap is NOT established. THE WARNING GOVERNS EVERY READING: Haiti was surveyed BY TELEPHONE, the Dominican Republic FACE TO FACE. A gap therefore mixes a difference between countries with a difference between instruments — people do not say the same thing to an interviewer at their door as to a voice on the phone. This product shows where to look, not what to conclude.
ds.prd054_h: Twenty years of public opinion — Haiti and the Dominican Republic
ds.prd054_meta: 📄 Société • Sources : LAPOP Lab, Vanderbilt University — AmericasBarometer 2006-2023 • confidence level A • Licence par clic LAPOP — agrégats autorisés, usage commercial interdit
ds.prd054_p: THE EXPLORATEUR'S FIRST LONG SERIES ON WHAT PEOPLE THINK. 1,494 estimates, nine waves from 2006 to 2023, the two countries of one island, nationally AND BY SURVEY REGION — trust in the courts, parliament, police and elections; corruption; insecurity as lived; the wish to leave. Thirty-nine series run past four points, the threshold below which a trend is only an optical illusion. WHAT IT SHOWS: Haitians' intention to emigrate climbs from 58 % in 2012 to 78 % in 2023, a continuous rise — while the Dominican figure swings between 29 and 44 %. AVAILABILITY IS MEASURED, NOT DECLARED: a question is only estimated where its code appears in that wave's official questionnaire, checked across seventeen of them. That is why crime victimisation does not go back before 2012. THE PRECAUTION THAT GOVERNS EVERYTHING: the collection mode changes mid-series — telephone for recent waves, face to face before — and a break in a curve may be a change of instrument rather than of opinion. Every row carries its mode so you can see it.
ds.prd055_h: The survey-results base — 2,132 indicators by region
ds.prd055_meta: 👥 Social • Sources : EMMUS / DHS Program — API des indicateurs et référentiel officiel • confidence level A • Libre d'usage, citation imposée par le producteur
ds.prd055_p: EVERYTHING THE DHS PUBLISHES BY REGION, no longer a handful of hand-picked indicators. 76,983 values, 2,132 indicators, four surveys from 2000 to 2016 — of which 1,521 indicators appear in at least three surveys, that is, form a SERIES. Twenty-three families: child health, nutrition, education, employment, water and sanitation, household living conditions, women's empowerment, domestic violence, child protection. WHAT EXISTS IS MEASURED, NOT DECLARED: an inventory accompanies the base and says, indicator by indicator, which surveys it appears in — an indicator seen once does not make a trend, and nothing in a file of values flags that to the eye. THE LABELS REMAIN IN ENGLISH and the column says so: machine-translating 2,132 indicator labels would produce methodological false friends. The twenty indicators carried on the map are translated one by one. AN ERROR CAUGHT ALONG THE WAY, and it shows what a control is worth: a first filter discarded rows carrying a « second variable », which deleted the entire CHILD MORTALITY family — whose label « ten years preceding the survey » is a reference period, not a breakdown. A filter that removes rows never breaks anything: it only makes the file smaller. THE LIMIT THAT GOVERNS EVERYTHING: the last survey dates from 2016-2017, and the API publishes a COMPLETE confidence interval on only 371 values: 77 others carry an upper bound with no lower bound, which is not one — comparing two regions two points apart is not permitted by these data.
ds.prd056_h: Which survey region contains which commune
ds.prd056_meta: 👥 Social • Sources : EMMUS / DHS Program — contours de l'enquête ; découpage administratif du référentiel Atmart • confidence level A • Libre d'usage, citation imposée par le producteur
ds.prd056_p: THE TABLE THAT MAKES SURVEY OUTCOMES READABLE COMMUNE BY COMMUNE. Twenty outcome maps existed and spoke only on the map: a commune's factsheet carried none of them. To carry them there, one must know which survey region contains which commune — and the DHS does not publish the list. TWO METHODS, IN THIS ORDER. Nine departments out of ten coincide exactly with a region: the assignment is administrative, therefore exact, for 120 communes. THE WEST IS THE ONLY HARD CASE — the survey splits it into the metropolitan area and the rest of the West, without saying where the line runs. THE SURVEY'S OUTLINE IS TESTED BEFORE IT IS BELIEVED: confronted with the 120 communes whose region is known in advance, it recovers them 120 times out of 120. It is that published calibration which licenses using it for the other 20. RESULT: 138 communes out of 140 assigned, and TWO LEFT EMPTY — Pétion-Ville and Kenscoff, which the outline separates by only 17 and 15 points. They come out with their reason written: filling them with the likeliest value would place unverifiable figures on a territory. WHAT A REGIONAL VALUE IS NOT: a measurement of the commune. The DHS does not sample at commune level, and every commune in a region shares the same figure — the `portee_de_la_valeur` column says so on every row.

rz.en1_l1: Honest description — distributions, extreme values, missing data shown as missing, never quietly filled in
rz.en1_l2: Comparisons — means (t, Welch), proportions (chi-square, Fisher exact), ranks (Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis), analysis of variance
rz.en1_l3: Multiple testing — Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg correction as soon as several hypotheses are tested on the same data, otherwise you end up “finding” pure chance
rz.en1_l4: Always three numbers — the effect size in its real unit, its confidence interval, and only then the p-value
rz.en2_l1: The model follows the variable — continuous: linear regression; binary: logistic (odds ratios and marginal effects); counts: Poisson or negative binomial; repeated observations: fixed or random effects
rz.en2_l2: Robust standard errors by default — HC0 to HC3, or clustered by branch, region or individual when observations are not independent
rz.en2_l3: Automatic diagnostics — heteroskedasticity (Breusch-Pagan, White), autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson), collinearity (VIF), functional form (RESET), residual normality (Jarque-Bera) — each warning comes with its remedy
rz.en2_l4: Causal designs — difference-in-differences, instrumental variables (2SLS, with a weak-instrument warning), panel fixed effects
rz.en3_l1: Time series — trend, seasonality, breaks, ARIMA and exponential smoothing, validated on a period held back
rz.en3_l2: Bayesian forecasting — the output is not a number but a distribution: you read the interval, not just the central point
rz.en3_l3: Updating — each new period tightens the forecast instead of recomputing everything from scratch
rz.en3_l4: Hierarchical models — a branch, area or batch with few observations borrows information from the others, instead of producing a wild estimate from three cases
rz.en4_l1: No result without its diagnostic — convergence, effective sample size, divergences, predictive checks: a result that fails its controls does not go into a report
rz.en4_l2: Sensitivity — what the conclusion becomes if you change the starting assumption, the period kept or the cases excluded
rz.en4_l3: Reproducible — every result can be replayed: the data at the time of computation, the method, the version, the person who validated it
rz.en4_l4: Readable without being a statistician — every output comes with a plain sentence saying what the figure means, and what it does not say
rz.en_d: Four families of questions, four families of methods. The tool picks, with you, the one that matches your question and the shape of your data — and rules out the one that does not.
rz.en_rule: ⚖️ The rule written into the tool: a result is called an effect only if a design is named and its key assumption stated. Everywhere else, the report says association. A coefficient is not causal because it comes from a regression — it is causal thanks to the design around it. That is the whole difference between a dashboard that impresses and a figure that holds up in front of an auditor, a credit committee or a peer reviewer.
rz.en_warn: ⚠️ What we do not promise. Rezilta replaces neither the regulatory validation of a banking risk model, nor an accredited laboratory system, nor an ethics committee. It supplies what those procedures demand and what is almost always missing: the audit trail, the written method, the diagnostics and reproducibility. The decision remains yours.
rz.end_d: The pilot programme is open to a few organisations. You bring a dataset and a question that matters, we bring the platform and the method — and you keep everything that is produced.
rz.end_t: Let us build it on your real data

rz.fq1_a: A project management tool tracks tasks, a spreadsheet displays totals. Rezilta links the raw data to the published figure, with the method and the diagnostic in between. That is the chain an auditor, a supervisory authority or a peer reviewer demands — and that no spreadsheet holds over time.
rz.fq1_q: How is this different from a spreadsheet or a project management tool?
rz.fq2_a: No, and that is precisely the point: Rezilta connects to your MySQL or SQL Server databases, generates your forms in XLSForm (Kobo, ODK, SurveyCTO, CommCare), and comes out as Excel, PDF or a Power BI model. The aim is to link what you already use, not to force you to replace it.
rz.fq2_q: Do we have to abandon Kobo, SurveyCTO, Excel, MySQL or Power BI?
rz.fq3_a: Two answers. First, minimisation: we only collect what serves a question. Second, hosting: installation on your own servers is provided for, for cases where the data may not leave the country or the internal network. In every case, personal data is kept separate from analysis data, access is partitioned, and nothing is resold or used to train a model.
rz.fq3_q: Our data is sensitive and cannot leave.
rz.fq4_a: Formation360 remains available for producing sessions and training materials. Rezilta takes over and widens the data and project side — sources, indicators, analysis, evaluation, reports — for any kind of organisation, not just training.
rz.fq5_a: Never. It proposes an analysis, a first draft of a narrative, an anomaly detection — every proposal is identified as such, and a person validates before it enters a report. Responsibility stays human.
rz.fq6_a: Yes. The Project module is an option, not the core. A bank, a laboratory or a sales department uses the three layers — foundation, analysis, delivery — without ever opening a logical framework.
rz.fq6_q: We do not run projects, only data. Is this for us?
rz.fq7_a: No. You ask the question, the tool proposes the method that matches your data and translates the result into plain language. But the script and the data are always available: anyone who wants to check, or redo the computation in R, can do so at any time.
rz.fq7_q: Do you need to code or to be a statistician?
rz.fq8_a: Not on its word — which is why every result arrives with its diagnostics, its written assumptions and its script. A conclusion that fails its controls is flagged, not dressed up. And when the data does not allow a conclusion, the tool is built to say so rather than produce a reassuring figure.

rz.q2_d: We describe, we do not model. Nobody knows whether the observed gap is real or noise, whether the rise will hold next quarter, or whether the factor being blamed is the one actually at work.

rz.q3_d: The same figures are retyped every month, with the same typing errors. And when someone asks where a figure comes from, the answer is reconstructed from memory.

xp.box_h3: What this explorer does — and what it does not
xp.box_p1: It shows the information currently documented by Atmart Data — not everything that exists about a commune. Everything runs in your browser: four public files and one map outline, no application server, no account, no advertising tracker. An anonymous and aggregated audience measurement counts uses (a search happened) without ever knowing who or what — no cookie, no identifier, no IP address kept, and the text you type never leaves your browser: full method. What you see, you can download as is from the catalogue and recompute yourself.
xp.box_p2: The commune is the most detailed territorial level of the public edition. Communal sections, populated places and detailed polygons are available in the Haiti Geo Pack. Definitions, methods and quality statuses are set out on the Backbone page.
xp.class_note: Departments and arrondissements have no values of their own: they are aggregated from their communes according to the rule written in the dictionary, and the number of documented communes is shown alongside. The + button adds a territory to the comparison.
xp.comp_note: Two to four territories side by side — communes, arrondissements or departments. Every value carries its reference year, and comparisons across different years are flagged rather than smoothed over.

xp.mil_l1: 2003 census (IHSI) — the last exhaustive demographic base.
xp.mil_l2: CNIGS / OCHA COD-AB — the administrative division valid as at 29 November 2018, republished on 26 January 2026. This is the one this explorer uses for this edition, because it is the only one providing official join codes and geometries. Used does not mean in force today : communes have been created since.
xp.mil_l3: Recent IHSI demographic estimates — they include communes created after 2018 and therefore show higher totals.
xp.mil_p1: Haiti does not have a single territorial reference set, but several vintages that coexist:
xp.mil_p2: Exact wording: this version of the Explorer covers the 140 communes of the 2018 CNIGS reference set. More recent vintages recognise additional communes. A territory absent from 2018 is not a territory that does not exist — it is absent from that vintage.
xp.mil_p3: For the Ouest department: the 2018 CNIGS reference set contains 20 communes. This number may differ in more recent reference sets. We obtained it by counting this file, not by taking it from a third party.
xp.mil_p4: The vintage correspondence table (CSV, 192 entities) gives, for each territory, its Atmart identifier, its p-code, its vintage, its validity dates and a divergence note. Today it holds only the 2018 vintage: the others will be added when we have the official files, not before.
xp.mil_p5: We do not pick a number in silence: the explorer counts what the reference set it loads actually contains, and names it. Communes created after 2018 will be added with their validity dates as soon as an official reference set publishes them with their codes, without rewriting history.
